about: Live test catalog, v2 (draft). capabilities = what a chat can contain (input / output / dialog), per provider. scenarios = multi-turn dialogs that exercise several capabilities at once; the same dialog runs on every provider (unless `providers` limits it). A run is one provider per day: research first, re-export of old test chats (features.json), fresh scenario chats in the test project, then the research result. Primary check: everything the chat shows on screen is in the export; plus audit, schema drift and the capability checks below. Prompts are in English (fewer tokens; nobody reads these chats).

modelTiers.about: Scenarios name a tier, not a model. TASK.md maps the tier to what the model picker shows on the day (names change); the report records the model that actually answered (from the export).

claude.reasoning: same model with extended thinking on

chatgpt.top: the Thinking model at its highest effort / Pro

scenarios.title: Las Vegas → Boston road trip with kids: constraints → map and photos → weather → hotels and car → day-by-day plan → shorter variants → plan document and calendar file

turns.say: Plan a road trip by car from Las Vegas to Boston for mid-August, 10-14 days. We're 2 adults and 2 kids, so at most 6-8 hours of driving a day. Nature first; cities only if they're really worth it. We've already seen Zion and the Grand Canyon (Bryce again is fine). Don't route through Yellowstone, stay in the US, and avoid the 100-mile border zone. Ask me questions if you need to.
turns.onQuestion: If it asks: we start August 12, prefer motels or hotels under $250/night, kids are 8 and 11, we like short hikes and viewpoints.

turns.say: What about Arches? Does it fit? Be realistic about time: a 'quick stop' at a park like that is half a day for us.
Show the main stops on a map, with a photo of each.
What's the weather usually like at Arches and in Colorado in mid-August? And what's the forecast for Moab for the next few days?
Find 3 hotels near Moab for 2 nights, August 14-16, 2 adults and 2 kids, with prices. Also check one-way car rental prices Las Vegas to Boston.

Now give me a day-by-day plan as a table: overnight town, leg in miles and hours, what we see that day. Then a table of all stops: photo, name, short description, Google Maps link, time needed. And a Google Maps route link with the stops.
What if we only have 8 days? Short version, and where would we sleep if we just drive to Boston as fast as possible?
Put the final 13-day plan into a document I can edit (in the document/canvas panel, not in the chat), and give me an .ics calendar file with the overnight stays.

scenarios.title: A real text document: write in the document panel → add a table → rewrite a section

turns.say: Write a one-page proposal for a loyalty program for a small neighborhood coffee shop. Put it in a document in the side panel (artifact / canvas), not in the chat.
Add a section 'Budget' with a table: item, monthly cost, notes.
Make the introduction two sentences shorter and add a 'Risks' section with three bullets.

scenarios.title: Code both ways: a function in the reply → a module with tests as a file → run the tests → change the file → download

turns.say: Write a Python function that parses durations like '1h30m' or '45s' into seconds. Just put the code in your reply.
Now turn it into a module with unit tests, as a separate file in the code panel (artifact / canvas), not in the chat.
Run the tests and show me the output.
Add support for days ('2d4h') and update the file.
Give me the final module as a file to download.

scenarios.title: A device from photos: identify → what the pins are → where to buy a programmer, as cards → wiring diagram

turns.say: I took apart this device. What is it, and what are the main parts on the board?
Here is the other side of the board. Describe the pinout of the pads on it and what I could do with them.
Where can I buy a cheap programmer for it with delivery to Europe? Compare 3 options as cards with prices.
Draw a diagram of how to wire those pins to the programmer.

scenarios.title: Sales data: numbers → chart → report file → fix the report

turns.say: Here are sales by region. Compute the totals and each region's share, as a table.
Plot a bar chart by region.
Make a report.md file with the table and conclusions that I can download.
Add a 'Recommendations' section with three bullets to the report.

scenarios.title: Landing page: HTML in the panel → change it → flow diagram

turns.say: Make a one-page landing for a coffee shop called 'Zerno': header, menu with prices, contacts. One HTML file, shown in the panel with a preview.
Switch to a dark color scheme and add a reviews section.
Draw a diagram of how a visitor gets from the home page to placing an order.

scenarios.title: Physics homework: formulas step by step → picture → quiz

turns.say: Explain how to compute how far a ball goes if thrown at 30 degrees at 15 m/s. Formulas, step by step.
Draw a picture of the trajectory with the quantities labeled.
Give me a short quiz: 3 questions on this topic with answer options.

scenarios.title: Documents: real PDF + notes + long pasted article + code → answers → summary → translation → code review

turns.say: From the PDF: which HR activities does the diagram on page 4 list, and what are the before/after examples on page 9? From the notes: what action items are on me?
Summarize this article in 5 bullets:
Translate bullet 5 into Ukrainian and German.
Review this code and find the bug.

turns.say: Recommend a beginner's book on the history of Rome.
Something shorter?

research.about: One per provider day, started first and collected at the end of the day. The provider researches its own chat features: the report tests research export, and its findings feed discovery. A finding becomes a capability only after a dialog shows it on screen and in the export.
research.prompt:
Research everything that changed in the {providerName} chat product (the web app at {appUrl}) between {since} and today.

Context: I maintain a browser extension that exports a conversation to Markdown. I need every change that affects what can appear INSIDE a conversation, so I can test that it is exported correctly.

Look for:
1. Response elements: cards and widgets (maps, places, routes, weather, products/shopping, hotels, flights, sports, finance), image results, source/citation chips, entity chips, quizzes, buttons, any interactive UI rendered in a reply.
2. Tools that put content into a chat: code execution and its output, charts, files created for download, documents / canvas / artifacts / side panels, image generation and editing, deep research reports, agents, apps and connectors whose results show up in the chat.
3. Inputs: new attachment types, how long pastes are handled, screenshots, camera, screen sharing.
4. Conversation structure: editing and branching, memory or personal-context references, projects, temporary chats.
5. Model or formatting changes that change how replies look (new markup, new layouts).

For each feature give: name; what the user sees in the chat; an example prompt that triggers it; availability (plan, region, platform) and the date it shipped; a source link. Prefer official release notes, help center articles and the official blog; mark third-party sources as such. Skip pricing, API-only and enterprise-admin changes.

End with one table: feature | what appears in the chat | example prompt | shipped | source.
research.since: the date of this provider's previous test window (tests/live/runs/); 3 months back on the first run

clarify.about: Deep research often asks questions or shows a plan before it starts. Answer from here; never leave it waiting.

answers.scope / product: The consumer web app (chat), all plans including free and paid. Not the API, not enterprise admin.
answers.time window: From {since} until today. Older features only if they changed in that window.
answers.depth vs breadth: Breadth: list every relevant change, a short paragraph each.
answers.format / language: A report in English, ending with the table described in the prompt.
answers.anything else: Use your best judgment and proceed.

clarify.planApproval: If it shows a research plan with a Start / Edit button (Gemini) or asks to confirm the plan, start it without edits.

fixtures.about: Upload files live in tests/live/fixtures/ (public repo, kept byte-identical by .gitattributes). Only files that may be published.
fixtures.vape-board-front.jpg: Disposable vape taken apart: board with display, heater, battery leads.
fixtures.vape-board-back.jpg: Same device, back: wireless charging coil.
fixtures.vape-board-pins.jpg: Back of the board: pads R V C D G, B+/B-, AC1/AC2, marking SY-DM4038.
fixtures.job-description-guide.pdf: 14-page HR guide (slides): diagram on page 4, before/after examples on page 9.
fixtures.long-article.md: ~14 thousand characters about the Linux file system layout, for the long-paste turn.
